novel_features.name: Vendor rollup
novel_features.description: Joins SAM registration, exclusions, USAspending recipient profile, open opportunities, and recent news mentions for one federal vendor (needs DATA_GOV_API_KEY for the SAM.gov tier; pre-sync awards/recipients/news for full coverage).
novel_features.rationale: Joins five local tables (entities, exclusions, recipients, opportunities, articles) that the upstream APIs never join together. Capture-mcp's get_entity_and_awards covers two of those tables; no tool covers all five.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When the user asks about one company in federal IT, this is the one-shot answer — saves a dozen API calls and the join logic.

novel_features.name: Recompete radar
novel_features.description: Lists federal IT awards whose period of performance ends inside a chosen window, joined to the incumbent's profile and to any follow-on RFP already posted on SAM (run `sync --resources awards` first).
novel_features.rationale: Local SQL on awards.period_of_performance_current_end_date plus cross-source join to live SAM opportunities; no API endpoint returns this view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets a BD analyst or reporter find contracts that are about to recompete before they show up as news.

novel_features.name: News-to-contract correlation
novel_features.description: Fetches RSS articles and links each one to the underlying contracts and opportunities by deterministic name-match against local recipient and agency tables (needs `news sync` plus `sync --resources recipients,agencies` for entity matches).
novel_features.rationale: Three orthogonal data surfaces (awards, opportunities, news) joined by a persisted tags table — no existing tool combines all three.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns a federal-tech news feed into a structured set of references to actual contracts and RFPs.

novel_features.name: Agency modernization view
novel_features.description: For one agency, returns open IT opportunities, recent IT awards, IT-NAICS spend trend, and recent news mentions in one composed view.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-table aggregation scoped to a curated IT-NAICS set; useful only because awards, opportunities, and articles are all in the same local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'what's happening in agency X on the IT side' in one call instead of three searches across three websites.

novel_features.name: Weekly BD digest
novel_features.description: One structured bundle: new awards in window, upcoming recompetes, open-opportunity hits, and recent news, scoped to a comma-separated NAICS list or a saved profile.
novel_features.rationale: Composes recompete + deadline + news-correlation outputs against a user-persisted NAICS filter stored in local config.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Drops a 2.5-hour Monday-morning BD ritual to a single command.

novel_features.name: Explain this headline
novel_features.description: Given a news article URL or headline string, returns the article's text plus the linked recipients and opportunities, with the matched mention spans.
novel_features.rationale: Looks up the article in local store, reads its persisted tags rows, returns linked records — pure local-data join after sync.
novel_features.why_it_matters: A reporter or analyst pasting a URL gets the contract context, not just the article text.

novel_features.name: Anti-hallucination code guard
novel_features.description: Resolves a plain term ('cloud', 'cybersecurity') to a NAICS or PSC code only if it matches a real row in the local reference tables; on miss, returns suggestions and exits non-zero rather than guessing.
novel_features.rationale: Existing autocompletes (cliwant) return permissive matches; this command refuses to guess so an agent can not silently query with a hallucinated code.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents hallucinate NAICS codes constantly; this turns a silent empty-result-set into an actionable error.

novel_features.name: Set-aside eligibility filter
novel_features.description: Filters open opportunities to those whose set-aside categories match the SAM-registered socioeconomic indicators of a given UEI (needs DATA_GOV_API_KEY plus `sync --resources entities,opportunities`).
novel_features.rationale: Joins SAM entity socioeconomic fields with opportunity set-aside taxonomy; no MCP cross-references the two.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Vendors only see opportunities they can actually bid on; saves time triaging.

novel_features.name: Vendor watchlist diff
novel_features.description: Persistent watchlist that returns the news articles touching a vendor since the last recorded watch-tick (use --peek to read without advancing).
novel_features.rationale: Persisted watchlist state plus a diff against prior sync snapshot; one-shot tools cannot do this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reporters and analysts watching dozens of vendors get only the article deltas they care about.

narrative.headline: Federal IT spending, opportunities, and news joined into one local store — searchable, scriptable, and agent-ready.
narrative.value_prop: pubsec-tech wraps USAspending.gov (federal awards), SAM.gov Opportunities (live RFPs), and federal-tech RSS feeds (Nextgov/FCW, FedScoop, CyberScoop, MeriTalk, GovExec Technology, Federal News Network, and more) behind a single Go CLI. Unique to this CLI: cross-source joins that the upstream APIs never expose together — vendor rollups, recompete radar, news-to-contract correlation, and anti-hallucination NAICS/PSC guards.
narrative.auth_narrative: USAspending and every RSS feed are free and keyless. SAM.gov Opportunities needs a free data.gov API key (https://api.data.gov/signup/) set as DATA_GOV_API_KEY. Without the key, USAspending and news commands still work; only SAM.gov commands raise a clear error directing the user to obtain a key.

quickstart.comment: Pull NAICS/PSC reference tables, top-tier agencies, and recent IT-NAICS awards into the local SQLite store. Required before search/digest/correlation commands.
Pull RSS articles from the seven enabled federal-tech feeds (Nextgov/FCW, FedScoop, CyberScoop, MeriTalk, GovExec Technology, Federal News Network) into the local store.
One-shot vendor rollup: SAM registration, exclusions, USAspending recipient profile, open opportunities, recent news mentions.
Find contracts ending in the next 18 months that match the NAICS, with the incumbent vendor's profile.
Last 7 days of federal-IT news with each article linked to the underlying awards and opportunities.
Single agent-readable digest: new opps, new awards, top headlines, deadlines this week.

troubleshoots.fix: Sign up at https://api.data.gov/signup/ (free), then `export DATA_GOV_API_KEY=<your-key>` and re-run.
Non-federal data.gov keys are capped at 1,000 req/day. Use `pubsec-tech sync --opps-only` overnight and then query local store rather than re-hitting the API.
GovTech is fronted by Cloudflare and blocks plain HTTP clients. Disable it via `pubsec-tech sources disable govtech` or set a browser-shaped User-Agent in config.

troubleshoots.symptom: `code resolve cloud` exits non-zero with 'no match'
troubleshoots.fix: That's intentional — the anti-hallucination guard refuses to invent NAICS codes. Look at the suggestions it returned, pick one, and re-run with the exact code.

troubleshoots.symptom: USAspending search returns an empty array but you expect results
troubleshoots.fix: Use `pubsec-tech code resolve` to confirm the NAICS/PSC code you passed actually exists, and confirm date format (`--fy 2025` not `--year 2025`).

narrative.when_to_use: Use pubsec-tech when you need to query federal IT spending, find live IT contract opportunities, or correlate federal-tech news with the underlying contracts. It is the right choice for any task that joins two or more of: USAspending awards, SAM.gov opportunities, and federal-tech news (Nextgov, FedScoop, CyberScoop, MeriTalk, GovExec, FNN). It is not the right choice for grants-only research (use Grants.gov directly), defense-specific operational queries (use Defense News + service-specific APIs), or state/local contract data outside the optional StateScoop/Route Fifty RSS sources.

recipes.title: Confirm a NAICS code before any downstream query
recipes.command: pubsec-tech-pp-cli code resolve "computer systems design" --kind naics --agent
recipes.explanation: Anti-hallucination guard: returns the canonical NAICS code (541512) or exits non-zero with suggestions if the term doesn't match a real row. Always run this before querying USAspending with a NAICS filter.

recipes.title: Daily digest scoped to your NAICS list
recipes.explanation: Composes recompete + news-correlation against the IT NAICS set in one structured response. Demonstrates --select with dotted paths to narrow the verbose digest payload to only the fields an agent needs.

recipes.title: Find recompete opportunities for IT services
recipes.explanation: Joins awards.period_of_performance_current_end_date with the incumbent recipient and any already-posted follow-on RFP.

recipes.title: Explain a news article
recipes.explanation: Returns the article plus the awards and opportunities it references, with the matched mention spans.

recipes.title: Triage open opportunities for a small business
recipes.explanation: Filters open SAM opportunities to those whose set-aside categories the entity actually qualifies for (8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone).
